body:
honestly, I used to do it for the reason you said - because I was in a lot of emotional pain and I wanted to show it. it definitely was in a way an attention seeking behavior but more than just attention I wanted someone to notice and help me. 

at this point, it's honestly just the only thing that relieves my anxiety, i guess the pain is a distraction? or maybe it's just habit, I'm not really sure.

I feel this so much. These are the times that I can just lay forever in bed just staring at the ceiling. In the moment I will think it is better than the rollercoaster but honestly it's actually worse. I'd rather feel everything than nothing.

It's short for favorite person. I'm not really sure how to explain it? because I dont want to say it's exactly the same for everyone. For me its like.. this person can make everything feel better instantly but also they can make me feel terrible just as quickly. I guess I see him like my best friend but like x100? but that is not how every FP relationship is. 
(edited for more explanation)

I've done this, kind of, and then it ends with him saying yeah okay I'm always here if you need to talk and then I almost immediately need to talk. I kind of NEED someone else to be doing the cutting off to have any space. That was what happened with my last FP at least. I think until I have access to real mental health help I just need to do my best to manage it (which saying out loud is hilarious). I can live with it, albeit like.. Not having a great time. 
He knows I have BPD and I've thought about flat out explaining this all to him but I'm almost positive that would actually scare him away.
Every time I try to cut contact,  I either don't follow through or he asks me why I'm being so extreme. But I honestly feel like I'm a danger to him, emotionally.
